DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation with Associated Femoral Neck Fracture.

The patient's presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg following a high-energy rear-end collision, combined with immediate severe groin pain and bilateral knee pain, is diagnostic. The "knee pain" is a common referred pain pattern in hip dislocations due to tension on the iliofemoral ligaments. I have already requested the Pelvis X-Ray to confirm the dislocation and rule out associated fractures; please await the imaging results to finalize the fracture status.
